analysis.purpose: Test fixture builder that scaffolds a minimal workspace package on disk (package.json + src/index.ts) so cli.test.ts can exercise multi-package workspace behavior (e.g. --package scoping) against a real filesystem tree instead of mocks.
responsibilities: Create the package directory under wsRepo/rel
Write a package.json with the given name and a fixed version
Write src/index.ts exporting a const named after `name` (dashes replaced with underscores) equal to 1

businessRules.rule: Package version is always hardcoded to 0.0.0
Exported const name replaces '-' with '_' so a package name like 'my-pkg' becomes the valid JS identifier my_pkg

invariants: The created fixture package always has exactly one exported const, equal to the literal 1
preconditions: wsRepo is a valid, writable directory (the workspace fixture root)
inputs: rel: string — relative path under wsRepo for this package
outputs: void — its effect is entirely the files it writes to disk
sideEffects: Creates directories and writes 2 files (package.json, src/index.ts) to disk
errorBehavior: No try/catch — mkdirSync/writeFileSync failures (e.g. permission errors) propagate as thrown exceptions
risks: A `name` containing identifier-invalid characters other than '-' (e.g. spaces, dots) would produce a syntactically invalid index.ts — only the '-' case is handled
whatToDistrust: 10 call sites unresolved — all Node fs/path/JSON built-ins (join, mkdirSync, writeFileSync, stringify, replace), not an indexing gap

nodes.name: Workspace package fixture scaffold
nodes.summary: Builds a minimal on-disk npm package (package.json + src/index.ts) for workspace-detection test fixtures.

evidence.why: writeFileSync calls at L283 (package.json) and L285 (src/index.ts) create the two fixture files
